text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers make changes to the code, automated builds start immediately. These builds compile the code and run tests to check that everything works correctly. The main goal is to catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear process: building, testing, and reporting results. If a test fails, the team knows right away and can fix the problem quickly. This saves time and helps teams work together more efficiently.
